# moddotplot-interactive v0.8.1

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

v0.8.1 makes frequently used palette choices faster to reach and adds direct control
over the direction and individual colors of the similarity display. It remains a
functional preview; these presentation changes do not alter numeric tiles or estimator
semantics. See the [validation record](v0.8.1/VALIDATION.md) for the completed local
verification evidence.

## Default Spectral direction

The initial similarity style remains 11-class Spectral on a white plot background, but
its direction is now reversed: lower displayed identity begins at purple and higher
identity reaches red. This is Spectral's palette-specific default in the application.
All other palettes begin in their canonical direction.

The direction button reverses the complete active class order without recomputing the
sequence comparison. Recoloring applies to cached interactive tiles and completed grid
previews; exported figures and their legends use the same resolved direction.

## Palette menu organization

The palette menu is ordered into these groups:

1. Spectral
2. Viridis
3. Sequential
4. Diverging
5. Qualitative

Spectral is removed from the later Diverging group so it appears only once. The last
three groups contain the remaining ColorBrewer schemes in their respective families.
Viridis is a separately sourced application palette and is not labeled as a ColorBrewer
scheme. Spectral supports its exact 3 through 11-class ColorBrewer variants. Viridis
supports 3 through 12 exact discrete samples from
[d3-scale-chromatic's published 256-color table](https://github.com/d3/d3-scale-chromatic/blob/main/src/sequential-multi/viridis.js);
no RGB interpolation is used.

## Compact direction and color controls

The **Distinct colors** input now uses half of its former row, with the
**Direction**/**Flip** button in the other half. The palette-specific count bounds still
update when the selected scheme changes.

Below those controls, one swatch appears for each active discrete class. Selecting a
swatch opens an editor with a browser-native **Color wheel** control, an editable
six-digit **Hex code** field, and **Reset color**. The exact native color-control
interface varies by browser and operating system. A selected replacement is applied
consistently to the interactive plot, retained grid previews, image exports, and export
legends.

Export provenance records the palette name, class count, direction, and resolved
ordered colors so a customized figure remains interpretable.
